1: [[espn:662|Paul Pierce]] and [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] traded big scoring nights, but Boston escaped Staples Center with a 112–111 victory. Pierce finished with 39 points, seven rebounds and four assists, while Bryant led all scorers with 40 points, eight rebounds and six assists. The one-point finish gave your first NBA game a memorable ending between two of the league’s oldest rivals.

The Lakers led 58–54 at halftime before Boston outscored them 37–24 in the third quarter, taking a 91–82 advantage into the fourth. [[espn:2422|Delonte West]] supplied 19 points and 10 assists, and [[espn:2757|Ryan Gomes]] added 19 points and 12 rebounds on 8-of-10 shooting. [[espn:831|Wally Szczerbiak]] contributed 16 points as the Celtics built enough offense around Pierce to withstand a late Los Angeles rally.

The finish remained in doubt until the final shot. A Gomes tip-in put Boston ahead 110–106 with 56.7 seconds left, but [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] completed a three-point play to tie the game at 111 with 15.3 seconds remaining. Pierce then drew a foul from Bryant and made the first of two free throws with 3.2 seconds left. He missed the second, giving the Lakers one last chance, but Bryant’s attempt from the top of the key missed at the buzzer. Boston survived despite scoring only 21 points in the fourth quarter.
2: [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] powered the Los Angeles Lakers to a 109–89 win over the Phoenix Suns at Staples Center, scoring 43 points with eight rebounds and five assists. The Lakers seized control early, opening with a 35–22 first quarter and extending the margin to 62–41 at halftime. Bryant did much of his damage at the foul line, converting 20 of 23 free throws.

Phoenix had its own standout performances: [[espn:510|Shawn Marion]] scored 29 points and grabbed seven rebounds, while [[espn:2167|Boris Diaw]] assembled an 11-point, 10-rebound, 12-assist triple-double. [[espn:2166|Leandro Barbosa]] added 16 points, but the Suns could not erase the early deficit. Phoenix won the third quarter 29–21, trimming the lead to 13 entering the fourth.

The Lakers answered with a 26–19 final period to complete the 20-point victory. [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] contributed 14 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists, [[espn:1823|Smush Parker]] added 12 points and eight rebounds, and [[espn:2027|Luke Walton]] collected eight points, 10 rebounds and six assists. Los Angeles finished the regular-season home matchup with an emphatic win over a Phoenix team it would soon face in the playoffs.
3: The Los Angeles Lakers ground out an 82–72 win over the Chicago Bulls at Staples Center in a defensive, low-scoring contest. Chicago led 21–19 after the first quarter, but the Lakers moved ahead 38–35 at halftime. [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] paced Los Angeles with 23 points, 10 rebounds and four assists, while [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] scored 18 points with four rebounds and four assists.

[[espn:2456|Andres Nocioni]] carried Chicago's offense, scoring a game-high 30 points and hitting six of nine three-pointers. [[espn:2429|Luol Deng]] added 13 points, and [[espn:885|Ben Wallace]] collected eight points and 12 rebounds. The Bulls stayed within three points entering the final period, trailing 62–59, but struggled to find offense down the stretch.

The Lakers held Chicago to 13 fourth-quarter points and finished with a 20–13 edge in the period. [[espn:2748|Andrew Bynum]] supplied 12 points, 13 rebounds and four blocked shots, helping Los Angeles win the rebounding battle 51–42. The Bulls shot just 27-for-80 from the field, while the Lakers survived 22 turnovers to secure their ten-point victory. Bryant's late free throws and an Odom dunk in the closing seconds put the result beyond reach.
4: The Clippers broke open a close game with a 34-point third quarter and defeated Sacramento 102–93 at Staples Center. Los Angeles held a narrow 46–45 halftime lead before outscoring the Kings 34–24 in the third, turning a one-point edge into an 80–69 advantage. [[espn:91|Elton Brand]] led the Clippers with 22 points and three blocks, while [[espn:497|Corey Maggette]] scored 21 off the bench.

[[espn:566|Cuttino Mobley]] added 17 points and six rebounds, and [[espn:1982|Chris Kaman]] supplied 14 points, eight rebounds and three blocks. [[espn:2393|Shaun Livingston]] directed the offense with five assists. Sacramento got a game-high 26 points from [[espn:61|Mike Bibby]], along with 15 points and five assists from [[espn:556|Brad Miller]], but could not erase the deficit after the Clippers' decisive third period.

The win gave Los Angeles a 13–16 record and reversed its 93–80 defeat in Sacramento a month earlier. The Clippers' balanced scoring complemented Brand's interior presence, while the Kings fell to 12–15 despite Bibby's scoring performance.
31: [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] took over after halftime as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Houston Rockets 104–88 at Staples Center. Houston led 52–51 at the break behind [[espn:1722|Yao Ming]], who had already collected 20 points and 10 rebounds. Bryant had 19 first-half points, setting up a duel between the two stars.

The third quarter decided the game. Bryant scored 22 points in the period, hitting nine of 13 shots, as Los Angeles outscored Houston 37–18 and turned a one-point halftime deficit into an 88–70 advantage. He finished with 43 points on 19-of-32 shooting, including three three-pointers, along with six assists. The Rockets never seriously threatened the lead in the final quarter.

Yao finished with 33 points and 16 rebounds on 16-of-25 shooting, but Houston received little scoring support beyond [[espn:11|Rafer Alston]]'s 12 points and six assists. [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] added 21 points and six rebounds for the Lakers, while [[espn:1823|Smush Parker]] supplied 15 points and 10 assists. The decisive third-quarter burst overshadowed Yao's impressive performance.
